title: a non-literal computed key selects no statically known member, so it is a type error rather than a compiler-recognized capability access
notes: The boundary of the computed-member family pinned by 05-context-rows/a-computed-context-access-charges-the-same-row and the nine cases with it. Those recognize `Clock["context"]()` because a LITERAL element access resolves to the same property symbol as `Clock.context()` — same member, same emitted call. A non-literal key resolves to nothing statically, so no recognizer may claim it, and the question this case answers is what happens instead: it fails closed, but through the stock TypeScript check of the EMITTED module rather than through any Smithers rule. `Clock` is a class with no string index signature, so indexing it with a `string` is TS7053 under `noImplicitAny` (which `strict` brings, and specification/compatibility.mdx lists `strict` as required). The `messageContains` is declared because the code alone would be satisfied by any implicit-any report, and what is being pinned is that the receiver has no such member to select. EVIDENCE, and the reason this case exists: FB-report.md §7.3 recorded this path as unpinnable — "not expressible as an `expect: \"diagnostics\"` corpus case, so no case can pin it in the current harness". It is expressible. Measured 2026-08-25 with `node conformance/runner/run.mjs --backend both --filter`: both backends report TS7053 at 8:10 and agree. A `TS` code here is exactly what the harness documents it for — Smithers keeps TypeScript's behavior on syntax it shares — and the emit-check audit in judge.mjs refuses to satisfy this expectation unless the emitted-TypeScript stage actually ran.
